name: Congenital Oculomotor Nerve Palsy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Oculomotor Nerve Palsy

criteria.description: Presence of oculomotor nerve palsy symptoms from birth or early infancy
Limited or absent movement of muscles innervated by the oculomotor nerve (medial rectus, superior rectus, inferior rectus, inferior oblique)
Congenital ptosis affecting the upper eyelid on the affected side
Variable pupillary involvement including anisocoria or fixed dilated pupil
Exclusion of acquired causes such as trauma, infection, or neoplasm

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Congenital onset of oculomotor nerve palsy symptoms with extraocular muscle paresis and ptosis, excluding acquired causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging to exclude acquired etiologies.

searchTerms: one-sided eye movement paralysis at birth
congenital nerve palsy affecting eye movement
birth defect causing eye muscle weakness

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital ptosis of the upper eyelid
Ophthalmoplegia involving medial, superior, and inferior rectus muscles
searchTerms: eye muscle paralysis affecting multiple directions
limited eye movement in several muscles
paralysis of eye muscles controlling gaze

common.symptomName: Hypotropia (downward deviation of the affected eye)
Limited adduction of the affected eye
Compensatory head posture (e.g., head tilt or turn)
searchTerms: head tilt or turn to compensate
abnormal head posture to help vision

occasional.symptomName: Facial asymmetry due to compensatory mechanisms
searchTerms: uneven facial features due to compensation
abnormal pupil reaction on same side
impaired light reflex in one eye

rare.symptomName: Synkinetic movements of eyelid or eye muscles
searchTerms: involuntary eyelid or eye muscle movements

imaging: MRI showing hypoplasia or absence of the oculomotor nerve
Brainstem imaging to exclude acquired lesions
genetic: Rare familial cases suggest possible genetic etiology though no specific gene identified
other: Electromyography may show denervation of extraocular muscles

distinguishingFeatures: History of trauma, infection, or vascular event

redFlags: Sudden onset of oculomotor palsy symptoms
references: Kline LB. Oculomotor nerve palsy. Neurol Clin. 1996;14(1):1-15.
